svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The genetic code: read each mRNA codon from the centre of the wheel outward."], [1, "AUG: first base A, second U, third G \u2192 methionine, the start codon."], [4, "GCA \u2192 alanine. Note all four GC_ codons code for alanine: the code is degenerate."], [7, "UUU \u2192 phenylalanine."], [9.5, "UGG \u2192 tryptophan, which has only one codon."], [12, "UAA is a stop codon: translation ends."]]
svg.title: The genetic code wheel
svg.desc: A codon wheel of all 64 mRNA codons, read from first base in the centre to the amino acid at the edge, with an mRNA sequence AUG GCA UUU UGG UAA translated step by step.
svg.text: Read from the centre outward: first base → second → third → amino acid. Standard code.

g.data-info: Centre ring: the first base of the codon (5′ end of the mRNA codon).
The outer ring gives the amino acid each codon codes for. 61 codons code for 20 amino acids; 3 are stop codons.
AUG codes for methionine and is the start signal for translation.

g.text: peptide bonds join the amino acids
UAA, UAG and UGA have no tRNA: a release factor ends translation

g.data-info: Triplet; degenerate (most amino acids have several codons, often differing only in the third base); not ambiguous (each codon means one thing); universal in almost all organisms.
g.text: degenerate: most amino acids have 2–6 codons
non-overlapping and read from a fixed start (AUG)
not ambiguous: each codon has one meaning
universal: the same in almost all organisms
Met (AUG) and Trp (UGG) have only one codon
